_: THE RECIPES of the assistant's Pine reference: one whole script per request family a formula cannot hold, with the words a member uses for it (`asks`). Each is run through the member's own paste path when the reference is generated (assistantPineReference.test.js); one that does not run fully is never shown to the assistant. The script turn is handed only the recipes whose `asks` its request names (api/services/pine_authoring.py). `chart` is the kind of chart a recipe says something on: the generator computes it on bars of that kind.

recipes.title: Zigzag by percent
recipes.shows: a state machine kept in `var`: the running extreme, its bar, and the direction; a leg is confirmed when price reverses by the input percent, and ONE line per confirmed leg is drawn from the last confirmed swing to the new one

recipes.title: Supply and demand zones
recipes.shows: a zone is a box from a confirmed pivot (known `right` bars late) one ATR deep, extended to the right; boxes are kept in arrays so a zone price closes through is deleted, and the oldest is deleted past the input count

recipes.title: Volume profile of the last N bars
recipes.shows: the range of the last N bars is cut into rows, each bar's volume is added to the row its close falls in, and each row is a box whose length is its share of the largest row; the point of control is PLOTTED so the script has an output besides its drawings. ⛔ THE WORK IS DONE UNDER `if barstate.islast` ON PURPOSE: it loops over past bars, which is too slow to repeat on every bar. A script that reads where the chart ends is drawn only on a FINISHED bar, so on a live chart this one appears when the newest bar closes

recipes.title: Session VWAP with its own deviation bands
recipes.shows: VWAP's own bands, worked by hand because `ta.vwap`'s three-value form is not served: three running sums restart on each new day (`var`, reset when the day changes), VWAP is the volume-weighted mean of hlc3 and the band is the volume-weighted standard deviation of hlc3 around it; no `fill` (a script that carries values in `var` is run bar by bar, and that run does not draw a fill between plots yet)

recipes.title: Divergence between price and RSI, pivot to pivot
recipes.shows: a divergence is read from one confirmed pivot of the oscillator to the one before it (`ta.valuewhen(found, x, 1)`): price makes a lower low while the oscillator makes a higher low; the pivot is known `right` bars late, so the mark is offset back to the pivot's own bar

recipes.title: Higher highs and higher lows, labelled
recipes.shows: each confirmed pivot is compared with the pivot of the same kind before it (kept in `var`) and labelled HH, LH, HL or LL at the pivot's own bar; the labels are kept in an ARRAY and the oldest deleted past the input count, so the run owns them and the chart never fills (at most two are added on a bar, so two `if` trim it); the trend state is plotted as 1, -1 or 0 so it can be screened and alerted on, and so is the size of the label list, a value taken from the list the drawings are in

recipes.title: Unfilled gaps as zones
recipes.shows: a gap is a bar whose low is above the high before it (or the reverse) by the input percent; its box is extended right and deleted on the bar that trades back through the far side of it; the number of gaps still open is plotted, a value taken from the lists the boxes are in

recipes.title: Linear regression channel with its own deviation
recipes.shows: the channel's bands are the deviation of price AROUND THE LINE (the root-mean-square residual over the window, by a loop), never a deviation of the close; `ta.linreg(src, n, 0)` minus `ta.linreg(src, n, 1)` is the line's slope per bar; no `fill` (a script with a loop is run bar by bar, and that run does not draw a fill between plots yet)

recipes.title: Schaff Trend Cycle, two stages
recipes.shows: two stochastic stages, each smoothed with a value CARRIED from the bar before (`var`, updated with `:=`): the first stage is where the MACD sits in its own range, the second where the smoothed first stage sits in its own; a flat range keeps the value before

recipes.title: Average return by day of the week
recipes.shows: statistics are worked over a FIXED window of the last N bars, by a loop: a running total kept since the first bar depends on where the chart's history starts, and this engine does not draw that on a chart that does not reach the listing; the best day's average is PLOTTED so the script has an output besides the table. ⛔ THE WORK IS DONE UNDER `if barstate.islast` ON PURPOSE: it loops over past bars, which is too slow to repeat on every bar. A script that reads where the chart ends is drawn only on a FINISHED bar, so on a live chart this one appears when the newest bar closes

recipes.title: Prior day's high, low and close as lines
recipes.shows: the prior day's values come from `request.security(syminfo.tickerid, "D", high[1])` and are PLOTTED as stepped lines (each needs a title); on a daily chart they are simply the bar before

recipes.title: VWAP anchored to a date the member picks
recipes.shows: the anchor date is three whole-number inputs compared with the bar's own `year`, `month` and `dayofmonth` (an `input.time` default is not held by this engine, so the date is not one setting); two running sums start at the first bar on or after that date, and nothing is drawn before it

recipes.title: Opening range of the first minutes
recipes.shows: the range is built while the bar is inside the opening minutes of the day (minutes since the day's first bar, kept in `var`) and held for the rest of the day; it is for intraday charts and says nothing on a daily one

recipes.title: Fibonacci retracement between the last two swings
recipes.shows: the last confirmed pivot high and pivot low are kept in `var` with their bars; each level's PRICE is worked out on every bar into an array; the lines and labels are made ONCE (kept in arrays) and MOVED on every bar with their setters, so nothing waits for the last bar and nothing is deleted and remade; and the 61.8% level is plotted so it can be alerted on

recipes.title: Trendlines through the last two swing highs and lows
recipes.shows: the last two confirmed pivots of each kind are kept in `var`; each side's line is kept in an ARRAY, deleted and made again when a new pivot arrives, and extended to the right; where each line stands on the current bar is plotted, so a break of it can be alerted on

recipes.title: Heikin Ashi candles, in their own pane
recipes.shows: each candle is made from the bar and the candle before it: its close is the average of the bar's four prices, its open is halfway between the open and close of the candle before (the first one uses the bar's own open and close), and its high and low reach the bar's high and low. The candles are drawn in their OWN pane under the chart (a script cannot replace the chart's candles). All three colours of a candle are written (body, wick and border): a candle given only one is drawn half in the chart's default colours

recipes.title: A shaded cloud between two exponential averages
recipes.shows: two plots kept in variables (`a = plot(...)`), both TITLED, and one `fill(a, b, ...)` between them whose colour says which average is on top; a fill between plots needs a script with no `var` in it

recipes.title: Volume so far today against the usual for this time of day
asks: volume at the same time of day
recipes.shows: today's running volume divided by the average, over the last N FINISHED days, of the running volume at the same bar of the day. Each finished day is one row of a flat array (`array.push` a fixed number of values per day, a short day padded with its own total; the oldest row trimmed with `array.shift` in a counted loop), today's row is rebuilt from `array.clear` at each day change, and nothing is drawn until N whole days are stored. The bars before the first day change may be part of a day and are never stored. An intraday chart only
